answer: A bonded reputation atlas makes Sybil attacks unprofitable: every agent stakes a deposit and builds a public record of completed work in a shared atlas. New identities wait behind a velvet rope, taking only tiny tasks until verifiable history accumulates. To bridge to high-value jobs, an agent must hold its bond for weeks, and cheating slashes it. Faking a hundred identities then costs a hundred bonds plus a hundred histories of real work, while an honest agent keeps its stake and earns fees. Attack cost scales linearly with the number of fakes, so farming identities stops paying.
